# @horizon-republic/nominal-types

> Runtime-validated nominal types for TypeScript. A type is a class with a rule: `new Email(text)` checks the text, and every `Email` you hold is valid. Two types don't mix at compile time even when they wrap the same kind of value. Every type is a Standard Schema and a Standard JSON Schema. Optional adapters connect types to ArkType, Zod, Valibot, NestJS, class-validator, Swagger, GraphQL, superjson, MikroORM, TypeORM, Drizzle and Sequelize.

This file describes version 3 and ships inside the package: `node_modules/@horizon-republic/nominal-types/llms.txt` matches the installed code. Every documentation page ships next to it, under `docs/`; the [Docs](#docs) section lists them.

## Rules for agents

- Use `Type.parse(input)` for input that may be wrong (requests, files, env, queue messages). It returns `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, issues }` and never throws.
- Use `new Type(value)` only where a bad value is a bug. It throws `NominalError`.
- Build schemas, rules and checks through the namespace `n`: `import { n } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types'`, then `n.object()`, `n.of()`, `n.union()`, `n.constraint()`, `n.oneOf()`, `n.matching()`, `n.satisfying()`, `n.hideValues()`, `n.plain()`, `n.isType()`, `n.isObject()`, `n.isConstraint()`. These functions have no top-level exports of their own.
- Check request bodies, configs and value objects with `n.object()` and `n.constraint()`. If the project already uses ArkType, Zod, Valibot or class-validator, keep it and use that library's adapter instead.
- Declare a type as a class: `export class Sku extends AnyString.subtype('shop.Sku', /^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$/u) {}`. Add behaviour as getters and methods in the class body.
- For strings, numbers, bigints and booleans, build on a base type (`AnyString.subtype(...)`, `PositiveInteger.subtype(...)`). Only types under a base type can be read from text by `fromString()` and `fromEnv()`. Use `Nominal(name, rule)` for objects (`n.object()`) and for types with no base.
- Name types with the part of the system in front and a dot: `'billing.InvoiceNumber'`. Each part holds letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A `/`, a space or an empty part throws `TypeError`. Built-in types are named `nominal.Email`, `nominal.Uuid` and so on. Name the class like the last part.
- Compare instances with `a.equals(b)`, never `===`. Read the plain value with `.value`. Arithmetic needs `.value` (`quantity.value * 2`); `>`, `<`, `Number(x)` and template strings work on the instance itself. The date and time types are the exception: `>` and `<` throw, so compare with `Temporal.Instant.compare(a.value, b.value)`.
- For dates and times use `Instant`, `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`, `PlainDateTime` from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/temporal`, never `Date` or a string type. On Node.js 22 and 24, `import 'temporal-polyfill/global'` first in the program; without `Temporal`, building a value throws `TypeError`.
- For money use `Money` (`{ amount: '12.34', currency: 'EUR' }`), and `DecimalString` for other exact decimals; never a `number`. Compute with `add()`, `subtract()`, `multiply()`, compare with `compare()`: `>` and `<` on a `DecimalString` compare text.
- For ids that name their kind, declare `class UserId extends TypeId.subtype('shop.UserId', TypeId.withPrefix('user')) {}` and make new ones with `UserId.generate()`.
- `n.matching()` takes a regular expression with no flag or only `u`. Other flags throw `TypeError`.
- Rules must be synchronous. An asynchronous Standard Schema throws `TypeError: <name>: asynchronous schemas are not supported` when a value is checked.
- Declare types holding passwords or personal data with `{ sensitive: true }`. Where messages leave the app, use `hideValues: true` on `NominalPipe` or `toGraphQL()`, or call `n.hideValues(issues)`.
- Install the peer package of an adapter yourself (`npm install zod`). Every peer dependency is optional; nothing loads until the adapter's entry point is imported.
- Don't write code for version 2.0.x. It had `NType()`, `Type.getPipe()`, types such as `FirstName` and `UUID`, and constructors that checked nothing. None of these exist in version 3. To port such code, follow `docs/guides/core/migrate-from-v2.md`.

## Install and entry points

```shell
npm install @horizon-republic/nominal-types
```

Node.js 22.12 or later. ESM (`import`) and CommonJS (`require`). Bundlers keep only the types and functions an app imports, when it loads the package with `import`. No dependencies: the Standard Schema interfaces are part of the package, exported as the types `StandardSchemaV1` and `StandardJSONSchemaV1`.

| Entry point | Exports | Peer package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types` | the core API and the built-in types | none |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/temporal` | `Instant`, `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`, `PlainDateTime` | none; needs `Temporal`: Node.js 26, or `temporal-polyfill/global` |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/arktype` | `toArk`, `fromArk`, `constrainArk`, `ArkSchema`, types `ArkField`, `Built` | `arktype` ^2.2 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/zod` | `toZod`, `constrainZod`, type `ZodField` | `zod` ^4 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/valibot` | `toValibot`, `constrainValibot`, type `ValibotField` | `valibot` ^1 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/class-validator` | `NominalField`, types `NominalFieldOptions`, `NominalTarget`, `TargetValue` | `class-validator` ^0.14 or ^0.15, `class-transformer` ^0.5.1 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/nest` | `NominalPipe`, `NominalSerializerInterceptor`, `NominalResponse`, `NominalResponseInterceptor`, types `NominalPipeOptions`, `NominalPipeTarget`, `NominalExceptionFactory`, `NominalResponseSchema` | `@nestjs/common` ^11 or ^12, `rxjs` ^7.2 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/swagger` | `applyNominalTypes`, `ApiNominalProperty`, `ApiNominalBody`, `ApiNominalQuery`, types `OpenApiDocument`, `ApiNominalBodyOptions`, `ApiNominalQueryOptions` | `@nestjs/swagger` ^11 or ^12 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/graphql` | `toGraphQL`, type `GraphQLOptions` | `graphql` ^16 or ^17 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/superjson` | `toSuperjson`, types `SuperjsonTransformer`, `SuperjsonValue` | `superjson` |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/mikro-orm` | `toMikroOrm`, types `MikroOrmOptions`, `MikroOrmType` | `@mikro-orm/core` ^7 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/typeorm` | `toTypeOrm`, type `TypeOrmOptions` | `typeorm` ^0.3.13 or ^1 |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/drizzle` | `toDrizzle`, types `DrizzleColumn`, `DrizzleOptions`, `DrizzleParams` | `drizzle-orm` |
| `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/sequelize` | `toSequelize`, type `SequelizeOptions` | `sequelize` ^6 |

## Which tool for which job

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| one value from outside, such as a route parameter | `Uuid.parse(input)` |
| only a yes or no, no instance needed | `Uuid.accepts(input)`, `schema.accepts(input)` |
| a request body or a message | `n.object({ ... }).parse(body)` |
| a rule across fields (end after start, guests ≤ capacity) | `n.constraint()` passed to `n.object()` |
| a value object of several fields | `class Stay extends Nominal('booking.Stay', n.object({ ... }, rule)) {}` |
| a PATCH body, or part of an object | `CreateOrder.partial()`, `.pick('a')`, `.omit('a')`, `.extend({ ... })` |
| one of several object shapes told apart by a field | `n.union('method', { card: n.object({ ... }), invoice: n.object({ ... }) })` |
| configuration from environment variables | `class Config extends Nominal('app.Config', n.object({ ... }).fromEnv()) {}`, `new Config(process.env)` |
| numbers or booleans from a query string or CSV | `n.of(PositiveInteger).fromString()` |
| a list, a missing value, `null` | `n.of(Tag).array({ max: 20 })`, `.optional()`, `.nullable()` |
| an existing ArkType schema | `toArk()` fields, `fromArk()` around the object |
| an existing Zod or Valibot schema | `toZod()` / `toValibot()` fields, `constrainZod()` / `constrainValibot()` for rules across fields |
| class-validator DTOs | `@NominalField(Type)` |
| NestJS parameters and bodies | `NominalPipe` |
| NestJS responses with class-transformer | `NominalSerializerInterceptor` in place of `ClassSerializerInterceptor` |
| a fast JSON response from parsed values | `schema.stringify(value)` or `Type.stringify(instance)`; `@NominalResponse(schema)` in NestJS; `JSON.stringify(n.plain(value))` for any value |
| an OpenAPI document from `@nestjs/swagger` | `applyNominalTypes(document)` |
| Swagger for a body or query value checked by `NominalPipe` | `@ApiNominalBody(schema)`, `@ApiNominalQuery(name, schema)` |
| a GraphQL scalar | `toGraphQL(Type)` |
| instances through tRPC or Next.js | `superjson.registerCustom(...toSuperjson(Type))` |
| a database column | `toMikroOrm`, `toTypeOrm`, `toDrizzle`, `toSequelize` |
| any other Standard Schema library | the type itself, or `n.of(Type)` where the library treats a function as its own construct |
| messages without personal data | `{ sensitive: true }`, `hideValues` |

## Core API

All from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types`. `n` is a namespace object: `import { n } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types'` gives every member below written `n.…`. `Nominal`, the built-in types, the classes and every TypeScript type are imported by their own names.

### Declaring types

- `Nominal(name, rule, options?)` returns a class to extend. `rule` is a `RegExp`, `n.matching()`, `n.satisfying()`, `n.oneOf()`, `n.object()`, `n.constraint()` or any synchronous Standard Schema. `options` is `NominalOptions`: `{ sensitive?: boolean, implies?: readonly AnyNominalType[] }`.
- `Type.subtype(name, rule?, options?)` makes a narrower type. Its instances pass where the parent is expected, not the other way round. It runs the parent's rules first. A rule that narrows the value, such as `n.oneOf()`, narrows the type of `value` too.
- `Type.variant(name, rule, options?)` makes a sibling: the same methods, its own rule in place of the source's, and the two don't mix.
- `implies: [OtherType]` in the options says every value of the new type passes `OtherType`. Its instances then pass for `OtherType` at compile time, for `instanceof` and for `equals()`, together with what `OtherType` implies. It is trusted, never checked: `OtherType.parse(instance)` checks the value again and returns an `OtherType`. A subtype keeps its parent's implied types; a variant drops those of the level it replaces. An entry that is not a nominal type, or a type whose instances have members the new type lacks, throws `TypeError` at declaration.
- `n.matching(pattern, description?, json?)` builds a rule from a regular expression. `description` completes "must be …" in messages. `json` adds JSON Schema keywords such as `format` or `examples`. Returns a `PatternSchema`.
- `n.satisfying(guard, description, json?)` builds a rule from a type guard `(value: unknown) => value is T`. Without `json` the type can't describe itself as JSON Schema. Returns a `PredicateSchema`.
- `n.oneOf(...values)` builds a rule for a fixed set of strings, finite numbers, booleans or `null`, compared with `===`. Returns a `OneOfSchema` (`values`, `accepts`); its values are `OneOfValue`. The value type is the union of the listed literals. Message `must be one of "draft", "paid" (was "lost")`, or `must be "admin" (was "user")` for one value. JSON Schema `{ type?, enum }`. An empty list, a repeated value, a bigint, `NaN`, an infinity or an object throws `TypeError`. It takes no enum object: spread `Object.values()` of a string enum, list the members of a numeric one.
- `n.isType(value)` tells whether a value is a nominal type class, also from another copy of the package.

```ts
import { AnyString, n, Nominal, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export class Sku extends AnyString.subtype('shop.Sku', n.matching(/^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$/u, 'a SKU', { examples: ['TEA-0042'] })) {
  public get category(): string {
    return this.value.slice(0, 3);
  }
}

export class Quantity extends PositiveInteger.subtype('shop.Quantity', n.satisfying((value: unknown): value is number => typeof value === 'number' && value <= 99, 'at most 99', { maximum: 99 })) {}

export class Password extends AnyString.subtype('shop.Password', /^.{12,}$/u, { sensitive: true }) {}

export class OrderStatus extends AnyString.subtype('shop.OrderStatus', n.oneOf('draft', 'paid', 'shipped')) {}

new Sku('TEA-0042').category; // 'TEA'
Quantity.parse(100); // { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must be at most 99 (was 100)' }] }
Password.parse('short'); // { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must be matched by ^.{12,}$ (was a string of 5 characters)' }] }
new OrderStatus('paid').value; // 'paid', typed 'draft' | 'paid' | 'shipped'
```

### Static members of a type

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `new Type(input)` | checks `input` and returns an instance; throws `NominalError`. Takes a plain value only. |
| `Type.parse(input)` | `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, issues }`; never throws |
| `Type.accepts(input)` | `true` when `parse()` would succeed, built without an instance or issues; doesn't run a constructor of your own; doesn't narrow `input` |
| `Type.stringify(instance)` | the JSON text `JSON.stringify()` writes for the instance, generated per type and faster; an object type's fields in declared order; throws `TypeError` for a value JSON has no text for |
| `value instanceof Type` | `true` for its instances and its subtypes' instances, also across `import` and `require` copies; reads the brand only, so a forged object passes; use `parse()` to know a value is valid |
| `Type.typeName` | the name, such as `'shop.Sku'` |
| `Type.rule` | the rule of the type's own level |
| `Type['~standard']` | the Standard Schema and Standard JSON Schema interface |
| `Type.subtype()`, `Type.variant()` | see above |

What `parse()` does with an instance: an instance of the same type or a subtype comes back as it is, if this copy of the package built it and its `value` is unchanged. An instance of a parent, a variant or another type under the same base type has its value checked against the type's rules. So does anything else that passes `instanceof`: an instance from another copy, one of another type with the same name, an instance whose `value` was reassigned, a forged object; `parse()` returns a new instance of the type. An instance of an unrelated type is rejected. A constructor of your own that changes the input makes `parse()` return the issues, never throw.

### Instance members

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `value` | the checked value; `readonly` in TypeScript (JavaScript can still assign it, and `parse()` then checks the instance again); an object value is frozen; the instance itself is not frozen |
| `equals(other)` | same type line and same value; deep for objects; `Uuid` ignores case |
| `toJSON()` | the value; big integer types write a decimal string; date and time types write their RFC 3339 text |
| `toString()` | the value as text; JSON for an object value; date and time types write their text |
| `[Symbol.toPrimitive]` | the value, so `>`, `Number(x)` and template strings work; an object or Temporal value throws `TypeError` outside a string |
| getters per field, `copyWith(changes)` | on types built on `n.object()`; `copyWith` returns a checked copy and throws `NominalError`, also for a key the object doesn't declare (`is not allowed`); it calls `new` on the instance's class with the whole changed object, so a constructor of your own must take that object first |
| `console.log()` form | `Uuid { value: '…' }` in Node.js and Bun; a sensitive type shows `Email { value: <hidden, a string of 16 characters> }` |

Methods of built-in types that return a changed copy, such as `canonical()`, `withTag()` and `withoutTag()`, return the class of `this`: a subtype stays a subtype, and its rules can refuse the new value with `NominalError`.

A field of an `n.object()` type can't be named `value`, `equals`, `copyWith`, `toJSON`, `toString` or `constructor`. `Nominal()` throws `TypeError` for such a field.

### Schemas

- `n.of(Type)` returns a `TypeSchema`, a plain Standard Schema object. Chain: `.array(options?)` with `ArrayOptions` `{ length?, min?, max?, unique? }` (`unique: true` refuses an item that `equals()` an earlier one: `must not repeat an item (was "a")` at the repeat's index, JSON Schema `uniqueItems`), `.optional()` (accepts `undefined`), `.nullable()` (accepts `null`), `.fromString()` (reads text first; only right after `n.of()`, and only for a type with a text form, else `TypeError`). Every call returns a new schema. `.parse(input)` returns `{ ok, value | issues }`. `.accepts(input)` returns `true` when `parse()` would succeed, without building the value. `.toPlain(value)` copies a value the schema gave with every instance replaced by its `toJSON()`, keeping only declared fields of an object in declared order; `JSON.stringify()` then runs at plain-value speed. `.stringify(value)` returns the JSON text of such a value, the same as `JSON.stringify(n.plain(value))` with only declared fields in declared order; a writer generated for the schema on the first call reads each trusted instance's checked value directly, faster than `JSON.stringify()` of the same values made plain; anything else (an instance from another copy, one whose `value` was reassigned, a plain value, a field from another library) goes through `JSON.stringify()`, so the text is always the same and always escaped. Without code generation it is `JSON.stringify(schema.toPlain(value))`. It throws `TypeError` for a value JSON has no text for, such as `undefined`.
- `n.plain(value)` copies any value with every nominal instance, at any depth and from any copy of the package, replaced by its `toJSON()`; arrays and plain objects are copied, other objects (`Date`, class instances) kept; never changes the input; a value that refers to itself throws `TypeError`. Its type is `Plain<Value>`. `JSON.stringify()` calls `toJSON()` on each instance and runs several times slower than on plain values, so convert large responses first.
- `n.object(fields, ...constraints)` returns an `ObjectSchema`. A field is a nominal type, an `n.of()` schema, another `n.object()` or any Standard Schema. A field whose schema accepts `undefined` may be missing; any other missing field reads `is required`. Only own keys of the input are read. Keys it doesn't declare are dropped silently. `.strict()` refuses them with `is not allowed`. `.fromEnv()` reads each field with a text form from a string, makes every field optional in the input type, so `new Config(process.env)` compiles, and hides the values in its messages. `.keys` lists the fields. Constraints run once every field is valid. A constraint that reads a field the object doesn't declare throws `TypeError` at declaration. The key `__proto__` is refused. Methods that return a new schema and keep `strict()` and `fromEnv()`: `.partial()` / `.partial('a', 'b')` (fields may be missing; a field given as `undefined` counts as missing; a constraint that reads such a field runs only when all of them are present), `.required()` / `.required('a')` (the reverse, also for fields whose schema accepts `undefined`), `.pick('a', 'b')` and `.omit('a')` (keep a constraint only when every field it reads is kept), `.extend({ ...fields })` (adds fields, replaces those of the same name in place, keeps constraints). A name the object doesn't declare, or no name for `pick`/`omit`, throws `TypeError`. The value types follow (`Partial`, `Pick`, `Omit`, merged).
- `n.union(key, { tag: n.object({ ... }), ... })` returns a `UnionSchema` (`key`, `tags`; a `TypeSchema`, so `.array()`, `.optional()`, `.nullable()`, a field of `n.object()`, a rule of `Nominal()`). The input's own `key` picks the variant, and only that variant checks the object. A missing tag, or one no variant has, is one issue under the key: `must be one of "card", "invoice" (was "cash")`, or `must be "card" (was …)` for one variant; tags are strings compared with `===`. The value holds the tag under the key first, also when the variant doesn't declare it (a field of that name in the variant is replaced by the tag); `stringify()` writes it first too, and writes an object with an unknown tag through `JSON.stringify()`. Schemas from `partial()`, `required()`, `pick()`, `omit()` and `extend()` stringify their fields in their own `keys` order. Its type is `UnionValue<Key, Variants>`, a union that narrows on `value[key]`; the input type is `UnionInput<Key, Variants>`; the variants map is `UnionVariants`. JSON Schema: `oneOf` of the variants, each with `properties[key] = { const: tag }` and the key required; for OpenAPI 3.0 `{ type: 'string', enum: [tag] }` and `discriminator: { propertyName: key }`. No variants, a variant that is not an `n.object()` schema, or a key that isn't a string or is `__proto__` throws `TypeError`.
- `n.constraint(fields, check, options?)` returns a `Constraint`, a rule across fields, like a SQL `CHECK`. `fields` lists the fields it reads with their types. `check` gets their values already checked and returns `true`, `false` or a message string. `options` is `ConstraintOptions` `{ path?, message? }`; `path` names the field the issue belongs to.
- `n.isObject(value)`, `n.isConstraint(value)` tell those apart.

```ts
import { AnyString, Email, n, Nominal, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

const withinCapacity = n.constraint(
  { guests: PositiveInteger, capacity: PositiveInteger },
  ({ guests, capacity }) => guests <= capacity || 'must not exceed the capacity',
  { path: 'guests' },
);

export const CreateBooking = n.object({
  customer: Email,
  guests: PositiveInteger,
  capacity: PositiveInteger,
  note: n.of(AnyString).optional(),
}, withinCapacity);

export class Stay extends Nominal('booking.Stay', n.object({ guests: PositiveInteger, capacity: PositiveInteger }, withinCapacity)) {
  public get free(): number {
    return this.capacity.value - this.guests.value;
  }
}

CreateBooking.parse({ customer: 'jane@example.com', guests: 3, capacity: 2 });
// { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must not exceed the capacity', path: ['guests'] }] }

const stay = new Stay({ guests: 2, capacity: 3 });
stay.guests; // PositiveInteger
stay.free; // 1
stay.copyWith({ guests: 5 }); // throws NominalError: booking.Stay: guests: must not exceed the capacity
```

Configuration:

```ts
import { AnyBoolean, n, Nominal, PositiveInteger, Url } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export class Config extends Nominal('app.Config', n.object({
  PORT: PositiveInteger,
  DEBUG: n.of(AnyBoolean).optional(),
  DATABASE_URL: Url,
}).fromEnv()) {}

const config = new Config(process.env); // throws one NominalError listing every bad variable
config.PORT.value; // 3000 for PORT=3000
```

### Errors and messages

- `NominalError` extends `TypeError`. Members: `typeName`, `issues` (`{ message, path? }[]`), and `message` such as `'nominal.Uuid: must be a UUID (was "x")'`, with a path in front of each issue that has one: `'booking.Stay: guests: must not exceed the capacity'`.
- A required `n.object()` field that is missing, `undefined` or only inherited from the prototype reads `is required` (fields are read as own keys only). This holds for `fromEnv()` and for adapters that run an `n.object()` schema.
- Messages read `must be <description> (was <value>)`, the value as it was given. A string is quoted, a number, bigint (`42n`), boolean or `null` written as is, an array as `array`, anything else by its kind (`object`, `undefined`). A string over 64 characters is cut: `(was a string of 30000 characters starting "<first 32>"…)`.
- A sensitive type writes the value by kind: `(was a string of 7 characters)`, `(was an empty string)`, `(was a number)`. `Email`, `IpAddress` (and the types under it) and `MacAddress` are sensitive. A `.fromEnv()` schema hides the values of all its fields the same way.
- `n.hideValues(issues)` returns the issues with the value at the end of each message hidden the same way. It reads `(was "x")`, the cut form `(was a string of N characters starting "x"…)` and Valibot's `received "x"`.
- Rules from other libraries keep their own messages.

### JSON Schema

- `Type['~standard'].jsonSchema.input({ target })` and `.output({ target })`. Targets: `'draft-2020-12'`, `'draft-07'`, `'openapi-3.0'`; any other throws `TypeError`.
- `title` is the type name. A type with several rules gets one schema merged from them (stricter bounds, `integer` over `number`, the narrower format); rules that don't fit together, such as two patterns, stay apart in `allOf`. Only examples the whole type accepts are kept; OpenAPI 3.0 gets one `example`, and an exclusive bound as `minimum: 0, exclusiveMinimum: true`.
- Patterns in schemas hold no lookaheads or backreferences, so RE2-based tools read them. `Email` and `SemVer` move their length checks to `minLength`/`maxLength`; `Email` and `Hostname` add a `not: { pattern }`.
- Big integer types: input is `anyOf` a decimal string and a safe integer; output is the string.
- `n.object()` output adds `additionalProperties: false`.
- A rule without JSON Schema throws `TypeError: <name>: the schema cannot describe itself as JSON Schema`.

### TypeScript types

`ValueOf<Schema>` (the value a schema gives: `type CreateBookingBody = ValueOf<typeof CreateBooking>`; give the type its own name, since Bun and SWC record a schema named like the type in Nest's parameter metadata), `InputOf<Schema>`, `Parsed<Instance>`, `NominalType<Name, Schema, Instance?>`, `NominalInstance<Name, Value>`, `AnyNominalType`, `NominalSchema<Input, Value>`, `NominalOptions`, `SubtypeOf<Parent, Name, Value?, Implied?>` (`Implied` is the union of the `implies` classes), `ImplyingType<Name, Schema, Instance, Implied>` (what `Nominal()` returns), `Narrowed<Instance, Value>`, `VariantOf<Source, Name, Implied?>`, `VariantInstance<Source, Name, Implied?>`, `Brand<Name>`, `Branded<Names>`, `BrandsOf<Instance>`, `Unbranded<Instance>`, `Immutable<Value>`, `ObjectInstance<Name, Input, Value>`, `ObjectCopy<Input>`, `ObjectRule<Input, Value>`, `ObjectSchema`, `ObjectFields`, `ObjectInput<Fields>`, `ObjectValue<Fields>`, `TextInput<Input>`, `TypeSchema`, `UnionSchema`, `UnionInput<Key, Variants>`, `UnionValue<Key, Variants>`, `UnionVariants`, `Plain<Value>`, `NominalTarget`, `TargetValue<Target>`, `ArrayOptions`, `Constraint`, `AnyConstraint`, `ConstraintField`, `ConstraintInput`, `ConstraintInputs`, `ConstraintValue`, `ConstraintValues`, `ConstraintOptions`, `ConstraintVerdict`, `StandardProps`, `StandardSchema`, `PatternSchema`, `PredicateSchema`, `OneOfSchema<Value>`, `OneOfValue`.

## Built-in types

| Type | Name | Accepts | Text form |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AnyString` | `nominal.AnyString` | any string | yes |
| `NonEmptyString` | `nominal.NonEmptyString` | a string other than `''`; never trimmed | yes |
| `NonBlankString` | `nominal.NonBlankString` | under `NonEmptyString`: a string with a character outside Unicode `White_Space` (U+0085 is white space, U+FEFF and U+200B are not); never trimmed | yes |
| `Email` | `nominal.Email` | an RFC 5322 dot-atom address, up to 254 characters; sensitive; `local`, `domain`, `mailbox`, `tag`, `withTag()`, `withoutTag()`, `canonical()`, `isSameMailbox()` | yes |
| `Uuid` | `nominal.Uuid` | a UUID in any case; `version`, `timestamp`, `isNil`, `isMax`, `canonical()`; `equals` ignores case | yes |
| `UuidV4`, `UuidV7` | `nominal.…` | under `Uuid`: RFC 9562 version 4 or 7, nil and max refused; `UuidV7#timestamp` is always a `Date`; `canonical()` keeps the type | yes |
| `Ulid` | `nominal.Ulid` | 26 Crockford base32 characters, first `0`–`7`, `I`/`L`/`O`/`U` refused, any case; `timestamp`, `canonical()` (uppercase); `equals` ignores case | yes |
| `TypeId` | `nominal.TypeId` | a TypeID (spec v0.3.0): `prefix_suffix`, prefix up to 63 of `a-z` and `_` (letter first and last) or none (then no `_`), suffix 26 lowercase base32 characters, first `0`–`7`, any 128 bits; `prefix`, `suffix`, `timestamp` (`undefined` unless version 7), `toUuid()` (throws `NominalError` for bits `Uuid` refuses), static `withPrefix(prefix)` (a rule: `class UserId extends TypeId.subtype('shop.UserId', TypeId.withPrefix('user')) {}`), static `generate(prefix?)` (new UUIDv7, ordered within a process; a subtype uses its fixed prefix), static `fromUuid(uuid, prefix?)` | yes |
| `ObjectId` | `nominal.ObjectId` | a MongoDB ObjectId, 24 hex digits in any case; `timestamp` (seconds), `canonical()` (lowercase); `equals` ignores case | yes |
| `SemVer` | `nominal.SemVer` | Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, no `v` prefix, up to 256 characters, numbers up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; `major`, `minor`, `patch`, `prerelease`, `build`, `isPrerelease`, `compare(other)` (precedence, build ignored), `isNewerThan(other)`; `equals` compares the text | yes |
| `Url` | `nominal.Url` | an absolute URL with any scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `file:` too; use `HttpUrl` for links), no spaces or control characters; `protocol`, `hostname`, `host`, `origin`, `pathname`, `searchParams`, `toURL()`, `canonical()` | yes |
| `HttpUrl` | `nominal.HttpUrl` | an http or https URL | yes |
| `CountryCode` | `nominal.CountryCode` | an officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or `XK` (Kosovo), upper case (`UK`, `EU` refused); `flag`, static `codes`; JSON Schema `enum` | yes |
| `CurrencyCode` | `nominal.CurrencyCode` | an ISO 4217 List One code, upper case, funds, metals, `XTS` and `XXX` included; `minorUnits` (`undefined` for `XAU`, `XXX`), `isFund`, static `codes`; JSON Schema `enum` | yes |
| `DecimalString` | `nominal.DecimalString` | an exact decimal as text: optional `-`, digits without leading zeros, optional `.` and digits, up to 100 characters, kept as written (`'1.50'`, `'-0'` pass; `+`, `.5`, `5.`, `1e3`, spaces refused); `sign`, `integerDigits`, `fractionDigits`, `toMinorUnits(scale)` (bigint; `RangeError` if a non-zero digit would be lost), static `fromMinorUnits(amount, scale)`, `compare(other)` (exact), `canonical()` (trailing zeros dropped, `-0` → `0`); `equals` compares the number | yes |
| `LanguageTag` | `nominal.LanguageTag` | a well-formed BCP 47 tag in any case that `Intl` also takes (`en_US`, `french`, `zh-yue`, `i-klingon` refused); `language`, `script`, `region`, `canonical()` via `Intl.getCanonicalLocales`; `equals` ignores case | yes |
| `MediaType` | `nominal.MediaType` | an RFC 6838 type/subtype with RFC 9110 parameters, no wildcards, no repeated parameter name; `type`, `subtype`, `suffix`, `essence`, `parameters`, `charset`, `isJson`, `canonical()`; `equals` ignores case of names, spaces and quoting | yes |
| `HexColor` | `nominal.HexColor` | `#` and 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex digits; `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha` (0–1), `canonical()` (lowercase 6 or 8 digits); `equals` compares channels | yes |
| `Base64` | `nominal.Base64` | RFC 4648 §4 base64, `=` padding required, pad bits zero, `''` accepted; `byteLength`, `toBytes()`; JSON Schema `contentEncoding: 'base64'` (`format: 'byte'` for OpenAPI 3.0) | yes |
| `Base64Url` | `nominal.Base64Url` | RFC 4648 §5 base64url, no padding, pad bits zero, `''` accepted; a sibling of `Base64`; `byteLength`, `toBytes()` | yes |
| `Hostname` | `nominal.Hostname` | an RFC 1123 host name: LDH labels up to 63, 253 in all, no trailing dot, last label not all digits, `xn--` labels must decode; `labels`, `canonical()` (lowercase), `toUnicode()`, `isSubdomainOf()` (itself included); `equals` ignores case | yes |
| `DomainName` | `nominal.DomainName` | under `Hostname`: two labels or more, top-level domain of letters or `xn--` | yes |
| `IpAddress` | `nominal.IpAddress` | IPv4 dotted quad without leading zeros, or any RFC 4291 IPv6 text without zone or brackets; sensitive; `version`, `toBytes()`, `canonical()` (RFC 5952), `isLoopback`, `isPrivate`, `isLinkLocal`, `isMulticast`, `isUnspecified`, `isGlobal` (IANA special-purpose registries; IPv4-mapped answers as its IPv4); `equals` compares the address | yes |
| `Ipv4Address`, `Ipv6Address` | `nominal.…` | under `IpAddress`, one version; `Ipv6Address.toIpv4()` for `::ffff:…` | yes |
| `IpPrefix` | `nominal.IpPrefix` | CIDR `address/length` with host bits zero (JSON Schema can't check those); `version`, `address`, `length`, `contains(address or prefix)`, `canonical()`; `equals` compares the network | yes |
| `Ipv4Prefix`, `Ipv6Prefix` | `nominal.…` | under `IpPrefix`, one version | yes |
| `MacAddress` | `nominal.MacAddress` | EUI-48: six hex pairs, all `:` or all `-`; sensitive; `toBytes()`, `isMulticast`, `isLocallyAdministered`, `canonical()` (lowercase, colons), `pattern`; `equals` compares bytes | yes |
| `Isbn` | `nominal.Isbn` | ISO 2108 ISBN-10 (mod 11, uppercase `X` last) or ISBN-13 (978, 979-1…9; 979-0 ISMN refused), compact digits only, hyphens and spaces refused (not stripped) with `must be an ISBN without hyphens or spaces`; `format` (10 or 13), `canonical()` (the ISBN-13), `toIsbn10()` (`undefined` for 979), `pattern`; `equals` holds between an ISBN-10 and its ISBN-13; JSON Schema can't check the digit | yes |
| `Issn` | `nominal.Issn` | ISO 3297 `NNNN-NNNC`, hyphen required, mod 11 check, uppercase `X`; `pattern`; JSON Schema can't check the digit | yes |
| `Gtin` | `nominal.Gtin` | GS1 GTIN-8, -12, -13 or -14 (EAN, UPC), digits only, mod 10 check, all zeros accepted; `format` (8, 12, 13, 14), `canonical()` (14 digits, zeros in front), `pattern`; `equals` compares the 14-digit form; JSON Schema can't check the digit | yes |
| `Isin` | `nominal.Isin` | ISO 6166: 2 letters, 9 letters or digits, Luhn check digit on letters as 10–35, upper case only, prefix not checked against countries (`XS` passes); `prefix`, `nsin`, `pattern`; JSON Schema can't check the digit | yes |
| `AnyNumber` | `nominal.AnyNumber` | any number | yes |
| `FiniteNumber` | `nominal.FiniteNumber` | a finite number | yes |
| `PositiveNumber`, `NegativeNumber`, `NonNegativeNumber`, `NonPositiveNumber` | `nominal.…` | a finite number `> 0`, `< 0`, `≥ 0`, `≤ 0` | yes |
| `Float32` | `nominal.Float32` | a 32-bit float | yes |
| `Latitude`, `Longitude` | `nominal.…` | under `FiniteNumber`: -90 to 90 and -180 to 180 degrees, ends included | yes |
| `Integer` | `nominal.Integer` | a safe integer | yes |
| `PositiveInteger`, `NegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonPositiveInteger` | `nominal.…` | a safe integer `≥ 1`, `≤ -1`, `≥ 0`, `≤ 0` | yes |
| `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32` | `nominal.…` | signed 8-, 16-, 32-bit integers | yes |
| `Uint8`, `Uint16`, `Uint32` | `nominal.…` | unsigned 8-, 16-, 32-bit integers | yes |
| `Port` | `nominal.Port` | under `Uint16`: a port from 1 to 65535, 0 refused | yes |
| `AnyBigInt` | `nominal.AnyBigInt` | a bigint, a decimal string up to 1000 characters, or a safe integer number; `value` is a `bigint`; `toJSON()` writes the decimal string | yes |
| `PositiveBigInt`, `NegativeBigInt`, `NonNegativeBigInt`, `NonPositiveBigInt` | `nominal.…` | a big integer `≥ 1`, `≤ -1`, `≥ 0`, `≤ 0` | yes |
| `Int64`, `Uint64` | `nominal.…` | signed and unsigned 64-bit integers | yes |
| `AnyBoolean` | `nominal.AnyBoolean` | `true` or `false`; from text only `'true'` and `'false'` | yes |
| `Money` | `nominal.Money` | a root built on `n.object({ amount: DecimalString, currency: CurrencyCode })`: JSON `{ "amount": "12.34", "currency": "EUR" }`, at most `minorUnits` digits after the point (any for `XAU`, `XXX`; not in the JSON Schema); getters `amount`, `currency`, `copyWith()`; `minor` (bigint; `TypeError` without minor units), static `fromMinor(minor, currency)`, `add`, `subtract`, `compare` (`TypeError` across currencies), `multiply(integer)`, `isZero`, `isNegative`, `canonical()` (currency digits), `format(locales?)` (`Intl.NumberFormat`, display only); `equals` ignores trailing zeros | no |

Dates and times, from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/temporal`. Each is a root; `value` is the Temporal object. Text is strict RFC 3339: upper-case `T` and `Z`, years 0000 to 9999, a real calendar day, seconds required, a fraction of 1 to 9 digits after a dot, no `:60`, no week or ordinal dates, no `[zone]`. Each also takes a Temporal object of its kind. `equals()` uses Temporal's `equals()`. JSON Schema carries `pattern` beside any `format`.

| Type | Name | Accepts | Text form |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Instant` | `nominal.Instant` | `2024-05-01T09:30:00Z` or `…+02:00` (offset required, up to `±23:59`), a `Temporal.Instant`; `toJSON()` writes UTC; `toDate()`; format `date-time` | yes |
| `PlainDate` | `nominal.PlainDate` | `2024-05-01`, a `Temporal.PlainDate` in the ISO calendar; format `date` | yes |
| `PlainTime` | `nominal.PlainTime` | `09:30:00[.f]` or `09:30`, no offset, a `Temporal.PlainTime`; no `format` | yes |
| `PlainDateTime` | `nominal.PlainDateTime` | `2024-05-01T09:30:00[.f]` or `2024-05-01T09:30`, no offset, a `Temporal.PlainDateTime`; no `format` | yes |

```ts
import 'temporal-polyfill/global';
import { Instant } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/temporal';

const sent = new Instant('2024-05-01T11:30:00+02:00');
sent.toJSON(); // '2024-05-01T09:30:00Z'
Temporal.Instant.compare(sent.value, new Instant('2024-05-01T10:00:00Z').value); // -1
Instant.parse('2024-05-01 09:30:00'); // { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must be an RFC 3339 date-time with Z or an offset (was "2024-05-01 09:30:00")' }] }
```

Implied types: types that accept every value of a type and that its instances pass for, besides the types above it. `PositiveNumber` → `NonNegativeNumber`; `NegativeNumber` → `NonPositiveNumber`; `PositiveInteger` → `PositiveNumber`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeNumber`; `NegativeInteger` → `NegativeNumber`, `NonPositiveInteger`, `NonPositiveNumber`; `NonNegativeInteger` → `NonNegativeNumber`; `NonPositiveInteger` → `NonPositiveNumber`; `Int8` → `Int16`, `Int32`, `Float32`; `Int16` → `Int32`, `Float32`; `Uint8` → `Uint16`, `Uint32`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Float32`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeNumber`; `Uint16` → `Uint32`, `Int32`, `Float32`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeNumber`; `Uint32` → `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeNumber`; `Port` → `PositiveInteger`, `PositiveNumber`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeNumber`, `Uint32`, `Int32`, `Float32`; `PositiveBigInt` → `NonNegativeBigInt`; `NegativeBigInt` → `NonPositiveBigInt`; `Uint64` → `NonNegativeBigInt`. No other built-in type implies anything, and `Latitude`, `Longitude` and `Port` are never implied.

A number type never converts its input: `PositiveInteger.parse('2')` fails; `n.of(PositiveInteger).fromString()` reads `'2'`. Big integer types are the one exception and take a decimal string. A number beyond 2^53 - 1 is refused by big integer types, since it may have lost digits.

## Adapters

### ArkType

```ts
import { type } from 'arktype';
import { fromArk, toArk } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/arktype';
import { Email, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export const CreateOrder = fromArk(type({ customer: toArk(Email), quantity: toArk(PositiveInteger), 'note?': 'string' }));

CreateOrder.parse({ customer: 'jane@example.com', quantity: 2 }); // { ok: true, value: { customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger } }
```

- `toArk(Type)` is an ArkType field checked with the type's rules and messages. Called alone, the ArkType object gives plain values.
- `fromArk(type, ...constraints)` returns an `ArkSchema` whose `parse()` gives `{ ok, value | issues }` with instances. It is a Standard Schema.
- `constrainArk(objectType, ...constraints)` attaches constraints to a nested ArkType object.
- ArkType morphs on a `toArk()` field and some union forms throw `TypeError` when `fromArk()` builds the schema.

### Zod

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';
import { constrainZod, toZod } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/zod';
import { Email, PositiveInteger } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export const CreateOrder = z.object({ customer: toZod(Email), quantity: toZod(PositiveInteger) });

CreateOrder.safeParse({ customer: 'jane@example.com', quantity: 2 }); // { success: true, data: { customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger } }
```

- `toZod(Type)` is a Zod field that gives an instance. Its JSON Schema comes from Zod's `z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: 'input' })`.
- `constrainZod(object, ...constraints)` attaches constraints. A constraint reading a key that `z.object` or `z.strictObject` doesn't declare throws `TypeError`.
- Zod's own `parse()` throws `ZodError`; use `safeParse()` for `{ success, data | error }`.

### Valibot

- `toValibot(Type)` is a Valibot schema that gives an instance: `v.object({ customer: toValibot(Email) })`.
- `constrainValibot(object, ...constraints)` returns `v.pipe(object, rawCheck)`. The same undeclared-key `TypeError` applies to `v.object` and `v.strictObject`.
- Valibot's `v.parse()` throws `ValiError`; use `v.safeParse()`. Valibot rules give no JSON Schema.

### class-validator

```ts
import { NominalField } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/class-validator';
import { Email, n, Uuid } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export class CreateOrderDto {
  @NominalField(Email)
  public customer!: Email;

  @NominalField(n.of(Uuid).array({ min: 1, max: 50 }))
  public items!: readonly Uuid[];
}
```

- `@NominalField(target, options?)` checks the property and, with `plainToInstance`, turns it into instances. `options.serialize(value)` sets what `instanceToPlain` writes. Messages carry the property path: `customer: must be an email address (was a string of 4 characters)`.

### NestJS

```ts
// main.ts
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NominalPipe } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/nest';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
app.useGlobalPipes(new NominalPipe());
await app.listen(3000);
```

```ts
// orders.controller.ts
import { Body, Controller, Get, Param, Post, Query } from '@nestjs/common';
import { NominalPipe } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/nest';
import { Email, n, PositiveInteger, Uuid } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';
import type { ValueOf } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

const CreateOrder = n.object({ customer: Email, quantity: PositiveInteger });
type CreateOrderBody = ValueOf<typeof CreateOrder>;

@Controller('orders')
export class OrdersController {
  @Get(':id')
  public find(@Param('id') id: Uuid): void {} // checked by the global pipe from the declared type

  @Get()
  public list(@Query('page') page?: PositiveInteger, @Query('ids', new NominalPipe(n.of(Uuid).array({ max: 100 }).optional())) ids?: readonly Uuid[]): void {}

  @Post()
  public create(@Body(new NominalPipe(CreateOrder)) order: CreateOrderBody): void {}
}
```

- `new NominalPipe(target?, options?)`. `target` is a nominal type, an `n.of()`/`n.object()` schema or any synchronous Standard Schema (a `fromArk()` schema, a Zod object). Without a target it uses Nest 12's `{ schema }` on the parameter if that is a nominal type or `n.of()` schema, else the parameter's declared type (a nominal type, or the `n.of()`/`n.object()` schema Bun and SWC record for a type alias named like the schema), and passes every other argument through. Safe to bind globally.
- Declared types lose array items and `?`: `Uuid[]` is not checked without a schema, and a missing value of a declared type reaches the handler as `undefined`. To require it or check a list, give the parameter its own pipe or a `{ schema }`.
- In a query string, a lone value for an array schema becomes a list of one, and a string for a number or boolean type is read as its value (`?page=2` gives `2`), unless `fromString: false`.
- Options: `fromString` (default `true`), `hideValues` (default `false`), `exceptionFactory(issues, metadata)` (default: `BadRequestException` with `{ statusCode: 400, error: 'Bad Request', message: ['id: must be a UUID (was "x")'] }`). In a microservice pass an `exceptionFactory` that returns an `RpcException`.
- Pipes never run on `@Headers()`. Without an interceptor, responses use each instance's `toJSON()`. A Fastify response schema (fast-json-stringify) mishandles instances: an `AnyBoolean` holding `false` is written `true`, and a nullable field or a date and time type fails with status 500. Put `@NominalResponse(schema)` on such a route, return `schema.toPlain(value)` or `n.plain(value)`, or use `NominalSerializerInterceptor`. In plain Fastify, set the route option `serializerCompiler: () => (data) => Order.stringify(data)` and keep the JSON Schema in `schema.response` for `@fastify/swagger`. Nest's `ClassSerializerInterceptor` writes instances as `{ "value": … }`; use `NominalSerializerInterceptor` in its place (same arguments: `app.useGlobalInterceptors(new NominalSerializerInterceptor(app.get(Reflector)))`). It writes every instance, at any depth, as its `toJSON()`, then runs class-transformer as before (`@Exclude()`, `@Expose()`, groups, `@SerializeOptions()`).
- `@NominalResponse(schema)` on a route (or `@UseInterceptors(new NominalResponseInterceptor(schema))` on a controller) writes the returned value with `schema.stringify()` and sends it as `application/json; charset=utf-8`, on Express and Fastify; `schema` is an `n.of()`/`n.object()` schema or a nominal type. Errors are written by Nest as usual; outside HTTP the value passes unchanged. It works next to a global `NominalSerializerInterceptor`, which leaves the text alone.
- Give a schema's value type its own name (`type CreateOrderBody = ValueOf<typeof CreateOrder>`). Under Bun and SWC, `order: CreateOrder` with a shared name records the schema object as the parameter type: `@nestjs/swagger` writes a broken `$ref` and a global `ValidationPipe` answers 500.
- Nest 12 `@Body({ schema: CreateOrder })` works only together with the global `NominalPipe`.

### Swagger

- `applyNominalTypes(document)` fills the schemas `@nestjs/swagger` leaves empty for nominal types with each type's OpenAPI 3.0 schema. Use it on the result of `SwaggerModule.createDocument()`. Two of your types with the same last part need different schema names: `@ApiSchema({ name: 'billing.Email' })`.
- `@ApiNominalProperty(target, options?)` writes the type's schema into a DTO property; `options` are `@ApiProperty()` options and win.
- `@ApiNominalBody(target, options?)` on the route writes the request body that `@Body(new NominalPipe(target))` hides from `@nestjs/swagger`. Options: `name` (lists an object schema under `components.schemas` and refers to it with `$ref`; otherwise inline), `description`, `required` (default: required unless the schema accepts `undefined`).
- `@ApiNominalQuery(name, target, options?)` on the route writes a query parameter with the whole schema: a list behind `new NominalPipe(n.of(Uuid).array({ max }))` keeps `items`, `format`, `pattern` and `maxItems`, which `@nestjs/swagger` loses. `@Query('page') page?: PositiveInteger` is shown required by `@nestjs/swagger`; write `@ApiNominalQuery('page', PositiveInteger, { required: false })` or pass `n.of(PositiveInteger).optional()`. Options: `description`, `required`.
- Types: `ApiNominalBodyOptions`, `ApiNominalQueryOptions`.
- Schemas are matched by class name, so a minified server build needs class names kept (esbuild/tsup `keepNames: true`, terser `keep_classnames: true`).

### GraphQL

- `toGraphQL(Type, options?)` returns a `GraphQLScalarType`. Arguments and variables arrive as instances; results are sent as `toJSON()`. Big integer literals keep every digit. Options: `name` (default: the last part of the type name, such as `Email`), `description`, `serialize`, `specifiedByURL`, `hideValues`. The scalar carries the type's JSON Schema in `extensions.jsonSchema`.

### superjson

- `superjson.registerCustom(...toSuperjson(Email))` keeps instances across tRPC and Next.js. Register each type once on both sides; subtypes need their own registration.

### Databases

| ORM | Use |
| --- | --- |
| MikroORM 7 | `email: p.type(toMikroOrm(Email))` in `defineEntity`, or `@Property({ type: toMikroOrm(Email) })` |
| TypeORM | `@Column(toTypeOrm(Email, { nullable: true }))` |
| Drizzle | `const email = customType<DrizzleColumn<typeof Email>>(toDrizzle(Email));` then `email('email')` in the table |
| Sequelize 6 | `email: toSequelize(Email)` as a model attribute |

- The column type comes from the nominal type: `Email` `varchar(254)`, `Uuid`, `UuidV4`, `UuidV7` `uuid`, `CountryCode` `varchar(2)`, `CurrencyCode` `varchar(3)`, `HexColor` `varchar(9)`, other strings with a length limit `varchar(<limit>)` (`Ulid` 26, `TypeId` 90, `DecimalString` 100, `ObjectId` 24, `SemVer` 256, `Isbn` 13, `Issn` 9, `Gtin` 14, `Isin` 12, `Hostname` and `DomainName` 253, `IpAddress` and `Ipv6Address` 45, `Ipv4Address` 15, `IpPrefix` and `Ipv6Prefix` 49, `Ipv4Prefix` 18, `MacAddress` 17), other strings `text`, integers `integer` or `bigint`, fractions `double`, `Int64` `bigint`, `Uint64` `decimal(20)`, `AnyBigInt` `varchar(1000)`, `AnyBoolean` `boolean`, `Instant` `timestamptz`, `PlainDate` `date`, `PlainTime` `time`, `PlainDateTime` `timestamp`. Override with `column` (MikroORM, Drizzle) or `type` (Sequelize) or TypeORM's own `type`. On PostgreSQL, choose `inet` for the IP address types, `cidr` for the prefix types and `macaddr` for `MacAddress`.
- Reads are checked; a stored value the type refuses throws `NominalError`. `trusted: true` skips the check.
- Writes store `toJSON()`, or `serialize(instance)`. `serialize` also runs on query values, and a plain value the type refuses (such as a `LIKE` pattern) is passed through.
- Sequelize `where` takes stored values, not instances.
- A driver's `Date` is read for `Instant` only, to the millisecond. For `PlainDate` and `PlainDateTime` make the driver return text (node-postgres: `types.setTypeParser(1082, (t) => t)`, `types.setTypeParser(1114, (t) => t.replace(' ', 'T'))`). With TypeORM store `PlainDateTime` as `{ type: 'varchar', length: 29 }`.
